blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules. Skip empty emails with `if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`; extract the seat filter into a named helper (e.g. `fn is_valid_seat(seat: &str) -> bool`, with a comment saying why a seat must contain '@') and the duplicated "add each valid seat, count it" loop of lines 19-26 and 31-36 into one function such as `add_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing) -> Result<usize, DbError>`, so each match arm is one call. Say in a comment why an existing account only gets new seats when its plan differs from the row (`if account.plan != row.plan`): a reader without the plan stumbles there and cannot tell whether that condition is intended or inverted — nor why the account's plan itself is never updated. The doc comment should also say that rows with an empty email are skipped and that seats without '@' are ignored.
findings.title: `import` nests five levels deep and hides its seat rules
